title: Post-Hoc Feature Selection Layer for Neural Networks Interpretability
abstract: arXiv:2610.31420v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: The interpretability of complex neural networks remains a critical challenge, especially for models already deployed in high-stakes domains. To address this, we adapted the Feature Selection Layer (FSL) to optimize feature weights post-training, a variant we term post-hoc FSL. Our approach reframes the FSL as a lightweight, trainable module that integrates with already frozen pre-trained models on tabular datasets to highlight the features the original model considers most important. This post-hoc FSL learns feature relevance by fine-tuning its weights based on the original model's learned outputs. Crucially, this process is non-invasive, operating without altering the original model's architecture or its learned parameters. translated_title: 用于神经网络可解释性的事后特征选择层
translated_abstract: 复杂神经网络的可解释性仍然是一个关键挑战，尤其是对于已经部署在高风险领域的模型。为了解决这一问题，我们将特征选择层（FSL）改造为在训练后优化特征权重的模块，并将其称为事后FSL。我们的方法将FSL重新构建为一个轻量级、可训练的模块，该模块与已冻结的预训练模型在表格数据集上集成，以突出显示原始模型认为最重要的特征。这个事后FSL通过基于原始模型学习到的输出微调其自身权重来学习特征相关性。至关重要的是，这一过程是无侵入性的，在不改变原始模型架构或其已学习参数的情况下运行。我们使用统计和视觉指标进行了实验，包括准确率、F1分数、召回率、精确率、加权t-SNE和轮廓系数，并分析了事后FSL在高维数据上的稳定性。
tldr: 提出了一种事后特征选择层，可在完全不改变已部署模型架构和参数的前提下，以无侵入的方式识别出模型认为最重要的特征，从而提升复杂神经网络的可解释性。
en_tdlr: Proposes a post-hoc Feature Selection Layer that non-invasively identifies the most important features of deployed models without altering their architecture or parameters, thereby enhancing the interpretability of complex neural networks.
